data.name: Liberty
data.gender_notes: Liberty is used as a unisex name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Latin word 'liber', meaning 'free'. The name Liberty represents freedom from oppression, tyranny, or bondage. It is a symbol of hope, courage, and resilience, reminding us to stand up for our rights and values. The name Liberty carries the meaning “Freedom from oppression” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Greek, Latin. Parents who choose Liberty usually hope their child will grow to embody freedom from oppression and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbol of hope and courage in the face of adversity
data.etymology: Liberty belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “Freedom from oppression.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Liberty total 1, giving a life-path number of 1. Number 1 is linked with Sun and with the qualities of leadership, independence and initiative.

data.cultural_impact: The name Liberty holds significant cultural impact as it is associated with the ideas of democracy, individual rights, and freedom. It is a name deeply embedded in American history, as symbolized by the Statue of Liberty, which represented the welcoming of immigrants to the United States seeking freedom from oppressive conditions. It is also a name associated with prominent political and social figures who advocated for human rights and freedom, such as the Liberty Tree in early American history.
data.spiritual_significance: The spiritual significance of the name Liberty lies in its reminder of the eternal goodness and freedom granted to us by God. It is a call to remember that no matter our circumstances, we are free from the bondage of sin and its consequences. It serves as a reminder to live our lives in accordance with God's will, and to steadfastly uphold our spiritual values and beliefs, despite any obstacles or challenges we may face. The name Liberty can serve as a source of courage and hope, encouraging us to trust in God's plan for our lives and to stand up for our faith and the freedom to practice it.

historical_references.reference: Historical records show that Liberty was the Roman goddess of freedom from bondage, both literal and metaphorical. The name Liberty carried significant spiritual weight in that era.
The Statue of Liberty, a gift from France to the United States, is named after the Roman goddess Liberty.
